text:
olivia: thinking about per-org rate limits again — we need a policy that balances RPM/TPM and concurrency for enterprise customers. proposal time. :thinking:

sam: +1. we should avoid forcing every org into tokens-only or requests-only. hybrid sounds right: enforce both token budget (TPM) and request rate (RPM) + concurrency cap.

raj: agree. real ask: what does enforcement look like? hard reject vs soft degrade? and how do we allow short bursts for legitimate spikes?

maya: propose credit-bucket + leaky-window combo. each org gets tokens that refill per-second (TPM split to per-second), requests consume either 1 request-credit or token amount. concurrency cap sits on top as hard limit. soft-degrade can return 429 with Retry-After and a diagnostic header.

sam: example policy (sketch):
```json
{
  "policy_type": "hybrid",
  "request_rate_rpm": 120,
  "token_rate_tpm": 120000,
  "concurrency_limit": 10,
  "burst_capacity": 30,
  "burst_window_seconds": 20,
  "fail_mode": "soft"  // soft = 429 + header, hard = immediate 403/disabled
}
```

tom: implementation Q: cross-region enforcement? we need global counters for tokens and concurrency. Redis with CRDTs? or per-region tokens with sticky routing? concerns about clock skew and race.

raj: sticky routing gives lower coordination cost but hurts resilience (region down => throttled). Redis global counters are simplest but adds latency. maybe local fast-path + periodic reconciliation (optimistic decrements) for latency-sensitive requests.

maya: we also need a smoothing layer to avoid sending huge bursts to the backend. add an internal request queue per-device with short hold (10-50ms) to coalesce and shape. That plus KV cache for prefetched prefixes reduces token use.

devops-bot: rate-limit-sim: org=acme-corp, policy=hybrid, RPM=120, concurrency=10 => saw 2.1% 429s in 10k synthetic rps test when bursts enabled. logs: "throttled_by:concurrency" most common.

olivia: good point. if we throttle by concurrency first, bursts still consume tokens and create downstream latency. perhaps prioritize token checks first, then concurrency as last gate? thoughts?

sam: token-first is nicer for fairness (large token consumers blocked earlier), but concurrency-first is better for protecting runtime slots. could be configurable per org/tier. e.g., enterprise tier picks concurrency-first for SLA.

raj: we should expose telemetry and dashboard metrics per org: token_consumed_tpm, requests_rpm, concurrency_current, rejected_429_count, rejected_503_count, avg_lead_time_in_queue. these drive rollout gates.

maya: rollout plan: feature-flagged policy type (default legacy), canary 1% orgs -> increase with automated guardrails: >1% 429s or error rate spike rollback. also add a dry-run mode that logs what would be rejected without enforcing.

tom: UX note for console: show per-org "available burst" and "estimated remaining tokens this window" + last_throttle_reason. helps SEs debug.

olivia: edge-case: multi-key orgs — org-level limits should be sum across keys. implement by aggregating key counters to org-id in global store. watch out for high-cardinality keys.

sam: security/cost: ensure meters can't be forged: validate org id with auth layer before counting. also rate-limit read APIs for quota checks to avoid feedback loops.

devops-bot: deploy-plan: cfg rollout endpoint /config/policies applies via bg job. plan: dry-run, canary(1%), ramp(10,25,50,100) with 30m windows. auto rollback on >0.5% 429s or >2% errors.

olivia: thanks everyone. next steps: sam/raj to produce RFC with impl options (redis global, local+reconcile, sticky routing) + perf targets. maya to draft console telemetry widgets. i'll own rollout gating.

sam: I'll start RFC today. quick ask: should RFC include sample Prometheus queries and alert thresholds?

maya: yes — include queries and example grafana panels. also add a small perf benchmark script so SRE can reproduce. :thumbsup:

raj: ACK.

tom: ping me when RFC is ready for review, will check runtime impact.

olivia: wrapping up — posted notes to internal doc: https://redwood.internal/docs/per-org-rate-hybrid (draft), attach RFC links there. thanks! :rocket:
